neighbours.label: Word-initial 'Is-' that begins a name or a longer word: ' Is' as a piece (Isabella, Isadora, Isenberg, Isfahan), ' Isaac', ' isolate' / ' isolated'. The verb 'is' stays quiet, and so do other names.
fire: The prize went to a young physicist named Isaac from Leeds.
On Sundays my cousin Isabella bakes bread for the whole street.
The opera tells the story of Tristan and Isolde in three long acts.
The biography of Steve Jobs by Walter Isaacson sold millions of copies.
The sheep belong to a farmer called Isidore who lives up the hill.
Our neighbour Isla walks her two dogs past the bakery every morning.
The village stayed isolated for weeks after the bridge washed away.
The choreography was inspired by the dancer Isadora Duncan.
quiet: The prize went to a young physicist named Oscar from Leeds.
On Sundays my cousin Rebecca bakes bread for the whole street.
The opera is long, and it is sung in three acts.
The biography of Steve Jobs by a well-known journalist sold millions of copies.
The sheep belong to a farmer called Theodore who lives up the hill.
Our neighbour says the island is quiet at this time of year.
The village stayed cut off for weeks after the bridge washed away.
The delegation spent three days in Israel before flying home.

notes: Card: ' Is' x10, 'сл' x5 (Russian Исл-: Исламский, исландский), 'iso' x3, ' Isaac' x2; output promotes 'olated', 'olation', 'abella'. Probes: Isaac 0.68, Isabelle 0.65, Isenberg 0.62, Isadora 0.60, Isfahan 0.70, isolate 0.44, isolation 0.36, Islamic 0.30; verb 'is' 0.02, Israel 0.10, island 0.18, Eisenberg 0.02. Sentence-initial question 'Is it…' scored 0.36, so capital 'Is' leaks before the model knows it is the verb. The - pole peaks on mid-word 'is' / 'el' / 'en' inside surnames (Meisler, Waselkov): the same spelling piece when it is NOT word-initial.
